speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The weather changes could have caused the tiles and the substrate to contract and expand at different rates, resulting in the loss of adhesion between the tiles and the substrate.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This phenomenon is not unique to Singapore and has also occurred in countries, such as Taiwan and Hong Kong.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Flat owners are responsible for maintenance of their own flats, including repairs for general wear and tear.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In private developments, developers generally only rectify dislodged tiles during the one-year defects liability period (DLP).

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Some developers may offer repair for dislodged tiles for a slightly longer period, for example, three years, but those are generally done on a goodwill basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: HDB has also worked with the Renovation Contractors and Materials Suppliers Association to compile a list of contractors whom residents can choose to engage on a private basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These are contractors who are able to repair the dislodged tiles at reasonable rates.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Grassroots organisations and Community Development Councils (CDCs) can also make use of existing local schemes to assist local residents who need financial help in this regard.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In all fairness, this is a generous goodwill offer.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have two further questions for the Second Minister.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I do have higher reported cases as well in the first two weeks of January.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, it was more than 30 cases reported.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I do notice that certain clusters of flats have more cases.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I want to ask the Second Minister if, indeed, it is a batch problem, whether it is a problem with quality or workmanship.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For a three- to four-room flat, with a household income of $2,000 to $4,000 a month, that is a major outlay.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If they are not lucky enough to have the tiles pop up before 15 years, they have to go and find ways to find cash to pay for it.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, would the HDB look at other ways to assist residents who are faced with such problems, because we do not want them to resort to licensed or unlicensed moneylending to fix the tiles.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Can HDB facilitate some kind of financing scheme, very much like how other agencies have done, like the small and medium enterprises financing or the Study Loan where we work with the financial institutions to do it?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Given that HDB does have the flat as a collateral, would the Second Minister consider this?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On second question, as I said earlier, if local residents face financial difficulties in dealing with popping tiles beyond the 15-year period, then they can approach their local CDCs and their local Grassroots Advisors to see if there are schemes that can assist them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are some CDCs that already have such schemes in place and these have been of great help to residents.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
